config.title: Restaurant Menu List

intro.title: Restaurant Menu List
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a restaurant menu list app that displays food items with their names, descriptions, and prices. You'll learn how to create and manage data arrays in TypeScript to store menu information. The main technologies involved are Ionic components for the UI, Angular for data binding, and TypeScript for type-safe data structures. By the end, you'll have a functional menu list that dynamically displays restaurant items in a clean, scrollable interface.
intro.usecase: This restaurant menu pattern is used in countless food delivery apps like Uber Eats, DoorDash, and Grubhub, where users browse categorized menus with item details and prices. It's also essential for restaurant POS systems where staff need to view available menu items during order taking. Similar list-category interfaces appear in e-commerce product catalogs, hotel service menus, and digital storefronts where items are organized into logical groups for easy navigation and selection.

objectives: Apply Ionic components to construct a structured restaurant menu interface
Implement Angular services to manage restaurant menu data retrieval
Use TypeScript interfaces to define the structure of menu item objects
Execute Angular data binding to display menu item properties in the template
Utilize Ionic list components to render a scrollable collection of menu items
Apply array iteration methods to traverse and display each menu item
Implement event handling to respond to user interactions with menu items
Control component styling by applying Ionic CSS utilities to menu elements
Construct a responsive layout that adapts to different screen sizes
Define component properties to store and manage the menu data state
Use Angular lifecycle hooks to initialize menu data when the component loads
Implement conditional rendering to display appropriate content based on data availability

steps.title: Import Ionic and Angular core modules
steps.instruction: Import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core', and IonContent, IonHeader, IonTitle, IonToolbar, IonList, and IonItem from '@ionic/angular/standalone'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple named exports from each package.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core'
// Import IonContent, IonHeader, IonTitle, IonToolbar, IonList, and IonItem from '@ionic/angular/standalone'
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have access to Angular's core decorators and Ionic's UI components for building the menu list interface.
successCriteria: The code should contain two import statements: one from '@angular/core' with Component and OnInit, and one from '@ionic/angular/standalone' with the six Ionic components listed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the necessary Angular and Ionic modules. This gives your component access to Angular's component decorator and lifecycle hooks, plus Ionic's UI building blocks.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your imports. Make sure you're importing from the correct packages and including all the required symbols: Component and OnInit from '@angular/core', and IonContent, IonHeader, IonTitle, IonToolbar, IonList, and IonItem from '@ionic/angular/standalone'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core', and IonContent, IonHeader, IonTitle, IonToolbar, IonList, and IonItem from '@ionic/angular/standalone' using TypeScript import syntax.

steps.title: Create the MenuItem interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named MenuItem with the following properties: id (number), name (string), description (string), and price (number).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.expectedOutcome: A MenuItem interface is created with proper TypeScript typing for menu item properties.
successCriteria: The interface must be named MenuItem and include all four required properties with correct types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the MenuItem interface with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your interface includes all four properties: id (number), name (string), description (string), and price (number).
steps.feedbackWrong: The MenuItem interface is not properly defined. Check that you used the 'interface' keyword, named it 'MenuItem', and included all required properties with correct types.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create the RestaurantMenuListComponent class with the @Component decorator. Set standalone: true and include the imported Ionic components in the imports array.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define your component. Remember to export the class so it can be used elsewhere.
steps.expectedOutcome: A RestaurantMenuListComponent class is created with the @Component decorator configured as standalone and importing the Ionic UI components.
successCriteria: The component class should be defined with @Component decorator, standalone: true, and include the imported Ionic components in the imports array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the RestaurantMenuListComponent with the correct standalone configuration and imports.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've included all required parts: @Component decorator, standalone: true, and the imports array with the Ionic components.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Make sure to use the @Component decorator with standalone: true and include the imported Ionic components in the imports array.

steps.title: Initialize menu items array
steps.instruction: Inside the RestaurantMenuListComponent class, add a property called 'menuItems' and initialize it as an empty array of type MenuItem.
steps.hint: You need to declare a property with the correct type annotation. Remember that MenuItem is the interface you defined earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a typed menuItems property ready to hold restaurant menu data.
successCriteria: The component class should contain a property declaration 'menuItems' with type 'MenuItem[]' initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully created a typed menuItems array property. This will hold the restaurant menu data that we'll display later.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there might be a small issue. Make sure the property is named 'menuItems', has the type 'MenuItem[]', and is initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The menuItems property isn't quite right. You need to add a property to the component class with the name 'menuItems', type it as 'MenuItem[]' (array of MenuItem), and initialize it as an empty array.

steps.title: Implement ngOnInit lifecycle hook
steps.instruction: Inside the RestaurantMenuListComponent class, implement the ngOnInit method to initialize the menuItems array with sample data. Populate it with at least three menu item objects that match the MenuItem interface structure.
steps.hint: The ngOnInit method is called automatically when the component initializes. Inside it, assign an array of objects to this.menuItems. Each object should have id, name, description, price, and category properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ngOnInit method is implemented and populates the menuItems array with sample data matching the MenuItem interface.
successCriteria: The ngOnInit method should assign an array of at least three MenuItem objects to this.menuItems. Each object must have all required properties (id, name, description, price, category).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the ngOnInit lifecycle hook to initialize your menu data. This ensures the data is ready when the component loads.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started implementing ngOnInit, but there are some issues. Make sure you're assigning an array of objects to this.menuItems, and each object should have all the properties defined in the MenuItem interface (id, name, description, price, category).
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnInit method isn't implemented correctly. Remember that ngOnInit is called automatically when the component initializes. Inside it, you need to assign sample data to this.menuItems. The data should be an array of objects that match the MenuItem interface structure.

steps.title: Add sample menu data
steps.instruction: Inside the ngOnInit method, assign the menuItems property with an array of 3-5 sample MenuItem objects. Each object should have id, name, description, price, and category properties.
steps.hint: Create an array literal with at least 3 MenuItem objects. Make sure each object matches the MenuItem interface structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ngOnInit method now populates menuItems with sample data, providing content to display in the upcoming UI steps.
successCriteria: The ngOnInit method should assign an array of MenuItem objects to this.menuItems. Each object must have id, name, description, price, and category properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added sample menu data. This provides realistic content for the restaurant menu list.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started adding data, but check that: 1) You're assigning to this.menuItems inside ngOnInit, 2) You have at least 3 MenuItem objects, 3) Each object has all required properties (id, name, description, price, category).
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnInit method should assign sample data to this.menuItems. Make sure you're creating an array of MenuItem objects with the correct properties.

steps.title: Set up the component template structure
steps.instruction: In the component's template property, add the basic Ionic page structure: an IonHeader containing an IonToolbar with an IonTitle, and an IonContent as the main content area.
steps.hint: The template should be a string containing Ionic components. Start with the IonHeader and IonContent elements.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of basic Ionic page structure in a component template
@Component({
  selector: 'app-example',
  standalone: true,
  imports: [IonHeader, IonToolbar, IonTitle, IonContent],
  template: `
    <ion-header>
      <ion-toolbar>
        <ion-title>Example Page</ion-title>
      </ion-toolbar>
    </ion-header>
    <ion-content>
      <!-- Main content goes here -->
    </ion-content>
  `
})
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a basic Ionic page structure with a header and content area ready to display menu items.
successCriteria: The template property should contain an IonHeader element with an IonToolbar and IonTitle inside, and an IonContent element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set up the basic Ionic page structure with a header and content area.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your template includes both the IonHeader (with IonToolbar and IonTitle) and IonContent elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure is incomplete. Remember to add both IonHeader and IonContent elements with the proper nesting.

steps.title: Add the menu list container
steps.instruction: Inside the IonContent component in your template, add an IonList component that will contain the menu items.
steps.hint: Add <ion-list> inside the <ion-content> tags. This will serve as the container for your menu items.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding IonList inside IonContent
<ion-content>
  <ion-list>
    <!-- Menu items will go here -->
  </ion-list>
</ion-content>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains an IonList component inside IonContent, ready to display menu items.
successCriteria: The IonList component should be added inside the IonContent component in the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the IonList container that will hold your menu items.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the IonList is placed directly inside the IonContent component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The IonList component needs to be added inside the IonContent component in the template.

steps.title: Create the menu item iteration
steps.instruction: Inside the IonList in your template, add an IonItem element with the *ngFor directive to iterate through the menuItems array. Display each menu item's name and price in the IonItem.
steps.hint: Use *ngFor="let item of menuItems" on the IonItem element. You can display the name and price using Angular interpolation: {{ item.name }} - ${{ item.price }}.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example of using *ngFor with IonItem -->
<ion-list>
  <ion-item *ngFor="let product of products">
    {{ product.name }} - ${{ product.price }}
  </ion-item>
</ion-list>
steps.expectedOutcome: The menu items from the menuItems array will be displayed as individual IonItem elements in the list, showing each item's name and price.
successCriteria: The IonList should contain an IonItem element with the *ngFor directive iterating through menuItems, and display each item's name and price using interpolation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the *ngFor directive to iterate through the menuItems array. Each menu item is now displayed as a separate IonItem in the list.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there might be an issue with the *ngFor syntax or the interpolation. Make sure you're using the correct syntax: *ngFor="let item of menuItems" and displaying the properties with {{ item.name }} and {{ item.price }}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The menu items are not being displayed correctly. Check that you've added the *ngFor directive to the IonItem element and are using the menuItems array from the component class.

steps.title: Display menu item details
steps.instruction: Inside each IonItem, display the menu item's name, description, and price using Angular interpolation syntax.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind each menu item property inside the IonItem element.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each menu item in the list will show its name, description, and price when the app runs.
successCriteria: The IonItem template should contain interpolation expressions for name, description, and price properties from the current menu item.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully used Angular interpolation to display menu item details. Each item now shows its name, description, and price.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some interpolation, but make sure to include all three properties: name, description, and price. Check that you're using the correct property names from the MenuItem interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: The menu item details aren't displaying correctly. Make sure you're using double curly braces {{ }} with the correct property names (item.name, item.description, item.price) inside the IonItem element.

steps.title: Format the price display
steps.instruction: In the template, use the currency pipe to format the price property as USD currency within the existing menu item details.
steps.hint: Use the Angular currency pipe with the 'USD' currency code. The syntax is {{ item.price | currency:'USD' }}.
steps.analogousExample: {{ product.price | currency:'USD' }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The price of each menu item should be displayed in USD currency format (e.g., $12.99) within the template.
successCriteria: The template must include the currency pipe applied to item.price with 'USD' as the currency code.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully formatted the price using the currency pipe. The prices now display in USD currency format, making them more readable for users.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the currency pipe isn't fully correct. Make sure you're using the syntax {{ item.price | currency:'USD' }} within the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The currency pipe isn't implemented correctly. You need to format the price property using the Angular currency pipe with 'USD' as the currency code.

steps.title: Add basic styling to the list
steps.instruction: Add the `lines='full'` attribute to the IonList component and the `lines='inset'` attribute to the IonItem component to apply proper visual styling.
steps.hint: Add the attributes directly to the Ionic components in your template. For IonList, use `lines='full'`. For IonItem, use `lines='inset'`.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example of adding lines attributes to Ionic components -->
<ion-list lines="full">
  <ion-item lines="inset">
    Item content
  </ion-item>
</ion-list>
steps.expectedOutcome: The IonList component will have full-width divider lines and the IonItem components will have inset divider lines, improving the visual appearance of the menu list.
successCriteria: The IonList component must have the attribute `lines='full'`. The IonItem component must have the attribute `lines='inset'`.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the lines attributes to the Ionic components. The menu list now has proper visual styling with full-width dividers for the list and inset dividers for each item.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but check that both attributes are correctly applied. Make sure IonList has `lines='full'` and IonItem has `lines='inset'`.
steps.feedbackWrong: The styling attributes are missing or incorrect. Add `lines='full'` to the IonList component and `lines='inset'` to the IonItem component.
